move: lock-screen notifications drop in from above, each pushing the stack down
how: A portrait iOS lock screen (aurora wallpaper slowly zooming 1.1 to 1.14 with a 2% vertical drift) with big clock and Dynamic Island. Four frosted notification cards start at y -70, scale .9, invisible; at 8%, 28%, 48% and 67% each one springs into the top slot with back.out(1.6) over 0.6s while every earlier card is pushed down one 196px slot with power3.out. The island squeezes scaleX 1.06 yoyo at the first arrival. At 85% the whole stack lifts 60px and fades with a 0.05s stagger, so the loop begins empty.
adapt: Replace the four app names, icons, messages and the wallpaper; change the arrival times via data-t and the slot gap (196px) to match card height; keep the back.out(1.6) 0.6s spring and 0.55s push.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the lock screen and N cards from shot.notifications with data-t fractions; animate returns the timeline placing each arrival at t*D and the clear at 0.85D. Uses backdrop-filter on the cards; scope the .note query to el.
